# Hiiaka and the industries that were always telling its story

The myths did not retire. They moved offices. This is the file on where **Hiiaka** works now.

The stories of Hiiaka place hula, magic, healing at the center of a living mythological world.

The [pattern atlas](/patterns/) — which maps every flagship temple to the industries its archetype demonstrably resonates with, each match argued and open to challenge — seats this temple in **4 industries**. This file reads those seats the way they were earned: through the myths.

## At a Glance

- **Temple:** Hiiaka
- **Pantheon:** Polynesian
- **Domain of influence:** Hula, Magic, Healing
- **Pattern seats:** 4
- **Sectors touched:** Health & Wellbeing
- **Strongest seat:** Healthcare, Pharma & Medicine
- **Series:** The Resonance Files, No. 208 of 542

## The Myth at Work

**Origins.** Hiiaka appears in polynesian tradition as hula, magic, healing.  The name's meaning, "patron goddess of Hawaiʻi", shapes the narratives told about this figure. — hold that image; the industries below are where it goes to work.

**Worship and Memory.** Devotees and later tradition-keepers preserved Hiiaka in ritual, text, and iconography, ensuring the name survived into the modern scholarly record. — that is not just a story. It is a business model, four thousand years early.

## The Long Employment

Hiiaka remains a touchstone for understanding polynesian religion, art, and identity. The age changed. The work did not.
